0Almost%20all%20the%20difficulty%20in%20real%20biomechanics%20comes%20not%20from%20those%20definitions%20but%20from%20measuring%20them%20well.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Challenge%200.**%20Before%20you%20begin%2C%20name%20one%20movement%20whose%20*speed*%20you%20would%20like%20to%20know%3A%20a%20sprint%2C%20a%20bicycle%20kick%2C%20a%20reaching%20movement%2C%20a%20car%2C%20an%20animal.%20Write%20down%20how%20you%20would%20measure%20it%20with%20the%20equipment%20you%20actually%20have.%20Keep%20it%20nearby%3B%20the%20last%20section%20asks%20you%20to%20come%20back%20to%20it.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20A%20measurement%20worth%20understanding%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Here%20is%20a%20plot%20of%20Usain%20Bolt's%20world-record%20100%20m%20final%20in%20Berlin%2C%202009%2C%20measured%20with%20a%20laser%20radar.%20The%20horizontal%20axis%20is%20where%20he%20was%20on%20the%20track%3B%20the%20vertical%20axis%20is%20how%20fast%20he%20was%20moving%20at%20that%20place.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cdiv%20style%3D%22background-color%3A%23F1F1F1%3Bborder%3A1px%20solid%20black%3Bpadding%3A10px%3B%22%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%3Cfigure%20aria-describedby%3D%22figure-caption-1%22%3E%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fimages%2Fusain_bolt_berlin2009.png%3Fraw%3D1%22%20width%3D700%20alt%3D%22Momentary%20velocity%20vs%20location%20for%20Usain%20Bolt%22%2F%3E%3C%2Ffigure%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%3C%2Fdiv%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cspan%20id%3D%22figure-caption-1%22%20class%3D%22figure-caption%22%20style%3D%22display%3Ablock%3Btext-align%3Acenter%3Bfont-style%3Aitalic%22%3E%3Cbr%3E%3Cb%3EFigure.%20Momentary%20velocity%20vs%20location%20for%20Usain%20Bolt%20in%20the%20men's%20100%20m%20final%20at%20the%20IAAF%20World%20Championships%20in%20Athletics%2C%20Berlin%202009.%20This%20measurement%20represents%20the%20velocity%20of%20the%20body%20(considered%20as%20a%20particle)%20and%20was%20measured%20with%20a%20laser%20radar.%20From%20%3Ca%20href%3D%22http%3A%2F%2Fwww.meathathletics.ie%2Fdevathletes%2Fpdf%2FBiomechanics%2520of%2520Sprints.pdf%22%3EGraubner%20and%20Nixdorf%20(2011)%3C%2Fa%3E.%3C%2Fb%3E%3C%2Fspan%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Look%20at%20it%20for%20a%20moment%20before%20reading%20on.%20A%20few%20things%20in%20that%20curve%20are%20worth%20noticing%2C%20and%20each%20one%20is%20a%20kinematic%20statement%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20-%20The%20velocity%20is%20not%20constant.%20He%20is%20still%20accelerating%20well%20past%20the%20halfway%20mark.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20The%20velocity%20peaks%20somewhere%20around%2060%E2%80%9370%20m%20and%20then%20*falls*.%20The%20fastest%20human%20on%20record%20was%20slowing%20down%20when%20he%20crossed%20the%20line.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20The%20curve%20is%20smooth%2C%20and%20its%20steepness%20at%20each%20point%20is%20itself%20a%20meaningful%20quantity.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20By%20the%20end%20of%20this%20notebook%20you%20will%20have%20reconstructed%20a%20coarse%20version%20of%20this%20plot%20yourself%2C%20from%20nothing%20but%20the%20ten%20split%20times%20published%20for%20that%20race.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Guiding%20questions%200.**%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20The%20vertical%20axis%20is%20velocity%20and%20the%20horizontal%20axis%20is%20position%20%E2%80%94%20not%20time.%20Is%20this%20a%20graph%20you%20could%20read%20off%20a%20stopwatch%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Roughly%20what%20is%20his%20top%20speed%2C%20in%20m%2Fs%3F%20Convert%20it%20to%20km%2Fh.%20Does%20the%20number%20surprise%20you%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20If%20he%20is%20slowing%20down%20over%20the%20last%2030%20m%2C%20why%20does%20nobody%20coach%20sprinters%20to%20%22just%20keep%20accelerating%22%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Python%20setup%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Two%20libraries%20carry%20most%20of%20this%20notebook%3A%20NumPy%20for%20the%20numbers%20and%20Matplotlib%20for%20the%20plots.%20We%20will%20add%20SymPy%20later%2C%20when%20we%20let%20the%20computer%20do%20the%20calculus%20for%20us.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20import%20numpy%20as%20np%0A%0A%20%20%20%20import%20matplotlib%0A%20%20%20%20import%20matplotlib.pyplot%20as%20plt%0A%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rc(%22axes%22%2C%20labelsize%3D13%2C%20titlesize%3D14)%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rc(%22xtick%22%2C%20labelsize%3D11)%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rc(%22ytick%22%2C%20labelsize%3D11)%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rc(%22legend%22%2C%20fontsize%3D11)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20np%2C%20plt%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Why%20mechanics%2C%20and%20why%20kinematics%20first%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**A%20good%20knowledge%20of%20mechanics%20is%20a%20necessary%20condition%2C%20although%20not%20a%20sufficient%20one%2C%20to%20master%20biomechanics.**%20For%20that%20reason%20we%20will%20review%20the%20principles%20of%20classical%20mechanics%20in%20the%20context%20of%20biomechanics%20rather%20than%20assume%20them.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20As%20argued%20in%20the%20notebook%20%5BIntroduction%20to%20Biomechanics%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fbiomechanics.py)%2C%20we%20begin%20with%20the%20branch%20of%20classical%20mechanics%20whose%20quantities%20are%20easiest%20to%20measure%20on%20a%20living%20system%3A%20kinematics.%20You%20can%20film%20someone%20sprinting%20with%20a%20phone.%20Measuring%20the%20force%20in%20their%20Achilles%20tendon%20while%20they%20do%20it%20is%20an%20entirely%20different%20undertaking.%20That%20asymmetry%20is%20why%20nearly%20every%20biomechanics%20curriculum%2C%20and%20this%20collection%2C%20starts%20here.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20There%20are%20relevant%20cases%20in%20the%20study%20of%20human%20movement%20where%20modeling%20the%20whole%20body%2C%20or%20one%20of%20its%20segments%2C%20as%20a%20*particle*%20is%20all%20you%20need.%20Performance%20in%20the%20100%20m%20race%20is%20one.%20The%20spatial%20and%20temporal%20description%20of%20a%20movement%20pattern%20is%20another.%20So%20is%20the%20minimum-jerk%20conjecture%20about%20how%20voluntary%20movements%20are%20planned.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20book%20%5B*Introduction%20to%20Statics%20and%20Dynamics*%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fruina.tam.cornell.edu%2FBook%2Findex.html)%2C%20by%20Andy%20Ruina%20and%20Rudra%20Pratap%2C%20is%20an%20excellent%20reference%20%E2%80%94%20rigorous%20and%20yet%20didactic%20%E2%80%94%20and%20freely%20available.%20Most%20of%20the%20content%20of%20this%20notebook%20is%20covered%20in%20its%20chapter%2012%2C%20and%20in%20chapter%201%20of%20Rade's%20book.%20Its%20preface%20and%20first%20chapter%20are%20a%20genuinely%20good%20read%20on%20*how*%20to%20study%20mechanics%3B%20do%20read%20them.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Guiding%20questions%201.**%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20For%20the%20movement%20you%20chose%20in%20Challenge%200%2C%20which%20is%20easier%20to%20obtain%3A%20its%20motion%2C%20or%20the%20forces%20that%20caused%20the%20motion%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Would%20treating%20the%20moving%20body%20as%20a%20single%20point%20throw%20away%20something%20you%20care%20about%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Kinematics%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Kinematics**%20is%20the%20branch%20of%20classical%20mechanics%20that%20describes%20the%20motion%20of%20objects%20without%20consideration%20of%20the%20causes%20of%20motion%20(%5BWikipedia%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FKinematics)).%20Kinematics%20of%20a%20particle%20is%20that%20description%20when%20the%20object%20is%20treated%20as%20a%20particle.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20A%20particle%2C%20as%20a%20physical%20object%2C%20does%20not%20exist%20in%20nature.%20It%20is%20either%20a%20simplification%20adopted%20to%20understand%20the%20motion%20of%20a%20body%2C%20or%20a%20conceptual%20definition%20such%20as%20the%20center%20of%20mass%20of%20a%20system%20of%20objects.%20Bolt%20is%20not%20a%20particle%3A%20his%20arms%20swing%2C%20his%20trunk%20rotates%2C%20his%20foot%20strikes%20the%20ground.%20But%20the%20laser%20radar%20in%20the%20figure%20above%20tracked%20essentially%20one%20point%20on%20his%20body%2C%20and%20for%20the%20question%20*how%20fast%20did%20he%20run*%20that%20was%20enough.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20This%20is%20the%20first%20modeling%20decision%20of%20biomechanics%2C%20and%20it%20is%20made%20silently%20far%20too%20often%3A%20**deciding%20what%20you%20are%20willing%20to%20ignore**.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Challenge%201.**%20Give%20one%20question%20about%20sprinting%20that%20the%20particle%20model%20can%20answer%2C%20and%20one%20it%20cannot.%20For%20the%20second%2C%20what%20would%20you%20have%20to%20add%20to%20the%20model%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Scalars%20and%20vectors%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Some%20mechanical%20quantities%20in%20kinematics%20%E2%80%94%20position%20and%20its%20derivatives%20%E2%80%94%20are%20vectors.%20Others%2C%20such%20as%20time%20and%20distance%2C%20are%20scalars.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20A%20**vector**%20in%20mechanics%20is%20a%20physical%20quantity%20with%20magnitude%20*and*%20direction%2C%20which%20also%20satisfies%20some%20elementary%20vector%20arithmetic.%20A%20**scalar**%20is%20fully%20expressed%20by%20a%20magnitude%2C%20a%20number%2C%20alone.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20distinction%20is%20not%20pedantry.%20%22He%20moved%20100%20m%22%20and%20%22he%20moved%20100%20m%20north%22%20are%20different%20claims%2C%20and%20only%20one%20of%20them%20lets%20you%20say%20where%20he%20ended%20up.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20For%20a%20review%20of%20scalars%20and%20vectors%2C%20see%20chapter%201%20of%20%5BRuina%20and%20Pratap's%20book%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fruina.tam.cornell.edu%2FBook%2Findex.html).%20For%20how%20to%20work%20with%20 ory%2C%20derived%20rather%20than%20recalled.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20A%20symbolic%20expression%20can%20also%20be%20plotted%20over%20a%20range%2C%20once%20the%20symbols%20have%20been%20substituted%20by%20numbers%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(a0_s%2C%20r0_s%2C%20r_s%2C%20t_s%2C%20v0_s)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20from%20sympy.plotting%20import%20plot%0A%0A%20%20%20%20r_num%20%3D%20r_s.subs(%7Br0_s%3A%201%2C%20v0_s%3A%202%2C%20a0_s%3A%204%7D)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20plot(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20r_num%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20(t_s%2C%200%2C%202)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20xlim%3D(0%2C%202)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20ylim%3D(0%2C%2010)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20axis_center%3D(0%2C%200)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20line_color%3D%22g%22%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20xlabel%3D%22Time%20%5Bs%5D%22%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20ylabel%3D%22r(t)%20%5Bm%5D%22%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20legend%3DTrue%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20title%3D%22Scalar%20kinematics%20of%20a%20particle%20at%20constant%20acceleration%22%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20backend%3D%22matplotlib%22%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20size%3D(5%2C%203)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20**Challenge%205.**%20Use%20%60sym.diff%60%20to%20go%20the%20other%20way%3A%20differentiate%20%60r_s%60%20twice%20with%20respect%20to%20%60t_s%60%20and%20confirm%20you%20recover%20%24a_0%24.%20Then%20try%20the%20same%20starting%20from%20a%20position%20that%20is%20*not*%20polynomial%2C%20such%20as%20%24r(t)%20%3D%20A%5Csin(%5Comega%20t)%24%2C%20and%20inspect%20the%20velocity%20and%20acceleration%20you%20get.%20What%20is%20the%20relationship%20between%20the%20position%20and%20the%20acceleration%20in%20that%20case%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Kinematics%20of%20human%20movement%3A%20the%20100%20m%20race%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Now%20we%20spend%20all%20of%20this%20on%20a%20real%20measurement.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20study%20of%20the%20biomechanics%20of%20the%20100%20m%20dash%20is%20a%20case%20where%20the%20analysis%20of%20the%20human%20body%20reduces%20honestly%20to%20the%20analysis%20of%20a%20particle.%20A%20technical%20report%20with%20the%20kinematic%20data%20for%20Usain%20Bolt's%20world%20record%20can%20be%20downloaded%20from%20the%20%5Bwebsite%20for%20research%20projects%5D(http%3A%2F%2Fwww.iaaf.org%2Fdevelopment%2Fresearch)%20of%20the%20International%20Association%20of%20Athletics%20Federations%3B%20%5Bhere%20is%20a%20direct%20link%20to%20the%20report%5D(http%3A%2F%2Fwww.iaaf.org%2Fdownload%2Fdownload%3Ffilename%3D76ade5f9-75a0-4fda-b9bf-1b30be6f60d2.pdf%26urlSlug%3D1-biomechanics-report-wc-berlin-2009-sprint).%20The%20table%20below%20shows%20the%20data%20for%20the%20three%20medalists.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cfigure%20aria-describedby%3D%22figure-caption-4%22%3E%3Ccenter%3E%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fimages%2FBerlin2009_100m.png%3Fraw%3D1%22%20width%3D700%20alt%3D%22Partial%20times%20of%20the%20100%20m%20race%20at%20Berlin%202009%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fcenter%3E%3C%2Ffigure%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cspan%20id%3D%22figure-caption-4%22%20class%3D%22figure-caption%22%20style%3D%22display%3Ablock%3Btext-align%3Acenter%3Bfont-style%3Aitalic%22%3EFigure.%20Data%20from%20the%20three%20medalists%20of%20the%20100%20m%20dash%20in%20Berlin%2C%202009%20(%3Ca%20href%3D%22http%3A%2F%2Fwww.iaaf.org%2Fdownload%2Fdownload%3Ffilename%3D76ade5f9-75a0-4fda-b9bf-1b30be6f60d2.pdf%26urlSlug%3D1-biomechanics-report-wc-berlin-2009-sprint%22%3EIAAF%20report%3C%2Fa%3E).%3C%2Fspan%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20column%20**RT**%20is%20the%20reaction%20time%20of%20each%20athlete.%20The%20IAAF%20rule%20on%20it%20is%20strict%3A%20any%20athlete%20with%20a%20reaction%20time%20below%20100%20ms%20is%20disqualified%2C%20on%20the%20grounds%20that%20no%20one%20can%20respond%20to%20the%20gun%20that%20fast%2C%20so%20they%20must%20have%20anticipated%20it.%20See%20%5BReaction%20Times%20and%20Sprint%20False%20Starts%5D(http%3A%2F%2Fcondellpark.com%2Fkd%2Freactiontime.htm)%20for%20a%20discussion%20of%20the%20rule%2C%20and%20you%20can%20measure%20your%20own%20at%20%5Bhumanbenchmark.com%5D(http%3A%2F%2Fwww.humanbenchmark.com%2Ftests%2Freactiontime).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Note%20what%20the%20reaction%20time%20does%20to%20the%20kinematics%3A%20the%20clock%20starts%20at%20the%20gun%2C%20but%20the%20athlete%20does%20not.%20Roughly%200.15%20s%20of%20Bolt's%209.58%20s%20were%20spent%20motionless.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Reconstructing%20the%20race%20from%20ten%20numbers%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Graubner%20and%20Nixdorf%20(2011)%20published%20the%2010%20m%20split%20times%20for%20that%20final%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cfigure%20aria-describedby%3D%22figure-caption-5%22%3E%3Ccenter%3E%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fimages%2FBerlin2009_100m_10.png%3Fraw%3D1%22%20width%3D600%20alt%3D%2210-m%20split%20times%20of%20the%20100%20m%20race%20at%20Berlin%202009%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fcenter%3E%3C%2Ffigure%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cspan%20id%3D%22figure-caption-5%22%20class%3D%22figure-caption%22%20style%3D%22display%3Ablock%3Btext-align%3Acenter%3Bfont-style%3Aitalic%22%3EFigure.%20Split%20times%20every%2010%20m%20for%20the%20three%20medalists%20of%20the%20100%20m%20dash%20in%20Berlin%2C%202009%20(Graubner%20and%20Nixdorf%2C%202011).%3C%2Fspan%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20That%20is%20all%20we%20have%3A%20eleven%20positions%2C%20eleven%20instants.%20No%20velocity%20was%20measured%2C%20and%20no%20acceleration.%20Everything%20else%20has%20to%20be%20computed%20with%20the%20two%20definitions%20from%20earlier%20in%20this%20notebook%20%E2%80%94%20each%20velocity%20as%20%24%5CDelta%20r%20%2F%20%5CDelta%20t%24%20over%20one%2010%20m%20segment%2C%20and%20each%20acceleration%20as%20%24%5CDelta%20v%20%2F%20%5CDelta%20t%24%20between%20consecutive%20velocities.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Before%20you%20run%20the%20next%20cells**%2C%20predict%20three%20numbers%20and%20write%20them%20down%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Bolt's%20average%20velocity%20over%20the%20whole%20race%2C%20in%20m%2Fs.%0A%20%20%20%202.%20His%20*peak*%20velocity%20%E2%80%94%20how%20much%20higher%20than%20the%20average%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20His%20peak%20acceleration%2C%20in%20m%2Fs%C2%B2.%20For%20scale%2C%20gravity%20is%20%249.8%5C%2C%5Cmathrm%7Bm%2Fs%5E2%7D%24.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.function%0Adef%20bolt_splits()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22Return%20the%2010-m%20split%20times%20of%20Usain%20Bolt's%20100-m%20world%20record.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Berlin%2C%202009%2C%20from%20Graubner%20and%20Nixdorf%20(2011).%20Returns%20the%20instants%20%5Bs%5D%0A%20%20%20%20at%20which%20he%20crossed%20each%2010-m%20mark%20and%20the%20corresponding%20positions%20%5Bm%5D%2C%0A%20%20%20%20both%20starting%20at%20the%20gun%20(t%20%3D%200%20s%2C%20r%20%3D%200%20m).%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20import%20numpy%20as%20np%0A%0A%20%20%20%20time%20%3D%20np.array(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%5B0.00%2C%201.88%2C%202.88%2C%203.78%2C%204.64%2C%205.47%2C%206.29%2C%207.10%2C%207.92%2C%208.74%2C%209.58%5D%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20position%20%3D%20np.arange(0%2C%20101%2C%2010%2C%20dtype%3Dfloat)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20time%2C%20position%0A%0A%0A%40app.function%0Adef%20split_kinematics(time%2C%20position)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22Average%20velocity%20and%20acceleration%20from%20split%20times%2C%20by%20finite%20differences.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Each%20velocity%20is%20the%20average%20over%20one%20segment%2C%20so%20it%20is%20attributed%20to%20the%0A%20%20%20%20midpoint%20in%20time%20of%20that%20segment%3B%20each%20acceleration%20likewise%20sits%20at%20the%0A%20%20%20%20midpoint%20between%20two%20velocities.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Returns%20(t_v%2C%20velocity%2C%20t_a%2C%20acceleration).%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20import%20numpy%20as%20np%0A%0A%20%20%20%20velocity%20%3D%20np.diff(position)%20%2F%20np.diff(time)%0A%20%20%20%20t_v%20%3D%20(time%5B%3A-1%5D%20%2B%20time%5B1%3A%5D)%20%2F%202%0A%0A%20%20%20%20acceleration%20%3D%20np.diff(velocity)%20%2F%20np.diff(t_v)%0A%20%20%20%20t_a%20%3D%20(t_v%5B%3A-1%5D%20%2B%20t_v%5B1%3A%5D)%20%2F%202%0A%0A%20%20%20%20return%20t_v%2C%20velocity%2C%20t_a%2C%20acceleration%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20bolt_time%2C%20bolt_position%20%3D%20bolt_splits()%0A%20%20%20%20bolt_tv%2C%20bolt_velocity%2C%20bolt_ta%2C%20bolt_acceleration%20%3D%20split_kinematics(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20bolt_time%2C%20bolt_position%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20print(%22Segment%20%20%20%20%20%20%CE%94t%20%5Bs%5D%20%20%20v%20%5Bm%2Fs%5D%20%20%20v%20%5Bkm%2Fh%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20for%20_i%2C%20_v%20in%20enumerate(bolt_velocity)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_dt%20%3D%20bolt_time%5B_i%20%2B%201%5D%20-%20bolt_time%5B_i%5D%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20print(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20f%22%7Bbolt_position%5B_i%5D%3A3.0f%7D-%7Bbolt_position%5B_i%20%2B%201%5D%3A3.0f%7D%20m%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20f%22%7B_dt%3A9.2f%7D%7B_v%3A10.2f%7D%7B3.6%20*%20_v%3A11.1f%7D%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20print()%0A%20%20%20%20print(f%22Average%20velocity%3A%20%7Bbolt_position%5B-1%5D%20%2F%20bolt_time%5B-1%5D%3A.2f%7D%20m%2Fs%20%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20f%22(%7B3.6%20*%20bolt_position%5B-1%5D%20%2F%20bolt_time%5B-1%5D%3A.1f%7D%20km%2Fh)%22)%0A%20%20%20%20print(f%22Peak%20velocity%3A%20%20%20%20%7Bbolt_velocity.max()%3A.2f%7D%20m%2Fs%20%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20f%22(%7B3.6%20*%20bolt_velocity.max()%3A.1f%7D%20km%2Fh)%2C%20%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20f%22around%20t%20%3D%20%7Bbolt_tv%5Bbolt_velocity.argmax()%5D%3A.1f%7D%20s%22)%0A%20%20%20%20print(f%22Peak%20acceleration%3A%7Bbolt_acceleration.max()%3A7.2f%7D%20m%2Fs%C2%B2%2C%20%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20f%22around%20t%20%3D%20%7Bbolt_ta%5Bbolt_acceleration.argmax()%5D%3A.1f%7D%20s%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20bolt_acceleration%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20bolt_position%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20bolt_ta%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20bolt_time%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20bolt_tv%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20bolt_velocity%2C%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20A%20few%20things%20in%20that%20table%20deserve%20to%20be%20read%20slowly.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20first%20segment%20is%20by%20far%20the%20slowest%2C%20and%20it%20is%20not%20close%3A%20about%205.3%20m%2Fs%20against%20a%20peak%20near%2012.3%20m%2Fs.%20Part%20of%20that%20is%20the%20reaction%20time%20sitting%20inside%20it%2C%20but%20most%20of%20it%20is%20simply%20that%20he%20started%20from%20rest.%20Sprinting%20is%2C%20for%20the%20first%2030%20m%2C%20mostly%20a%20problem%20of%20acceleration.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20peak%20velocity%20of%20roughly%2012.3%20m%2Fs%20is%20about%2044%20km%2Fh%2C%20and%20it%20is%20reached%20somewhere%20past%2060%20m%20%E2%80%94%20remarkably%20late.%20Then%20it%20falls.%20Bolt%20was%20*slowing%20down*%20over%20the%20last%2020%20m%20of%20the%20fastest%20100%20m%20ever%20run%2C%20and%20so%20was%20everyone%20else%20in%20that%20final.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20His%20average%20over%20the%20whole%20race%2C%20about%2010.4%20m%2Fs%2C%20describes%20no%20particular%20moment%20of%20it.%20It%20is%20the%20number%20that%20gets%20printed%2C%20and%20it%20is%20the%20least%20informative%20one%20in%20the%20table.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Now%20the%20same%20numbers%20as%20plots%2C%20including%20the%20velocity-against-position%20panel%20that%20reproduces%2C%20coarsely%2C%20the%20figure%20that%20opened%20this%20notebook.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.function%0Adef%20plot_sprint(time%2C%20position%2C%20t_v%2C%20velocity%2C%20t_a%2C% _acceleration%2C%0A%20%20%20%20bolt_position%2C%0A%20%20%20%20bolt_ta%2C%0A%20%20%20%20bolt_time%2C%0A%20%20%20%20bolt_tv%2C%0A%20%20%20%20bolt_velocity%2C%0A)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20plot_sprint(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20bolt_time%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20bolt_position%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20bolt_tv%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20bolt_velocity%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20bolt_ta%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20bolt_acceleration%2C%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20Compare%20the%20bottom-right%20panel%20with%20the%20laser-radar%20figure%20at%20the%20top%20of%20this%20notebook.%20The%20shape%20is%20right%20%E2%80%94%20a%20fast%20rise%2C%20a%20flat%20maximum%20past%20halfway%2C%20a%20decline%20to%20the%20finish%20%E2%80%94%20but%20ours%20is%20built%20from%20ten%20averages%20and%20theirs%20from%20a%20continuous%20measurement.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20That%20comparison%20is%20the%20honest%20lesson%20of%20this%20section%2C%20and%20it%20is%20worth%20stating%20plainly.%20**Every%20derivative%20we%20computed%20is%20a%20finite%20difference%20over%20a%20coarse%20interval%2C%20and%20each%20one%20is%20noisier%20than%20the%20one%20before%20it.**%20The%20position%20data%20are%20excellent.%20The%20velocities%2C%20averaged%20over%20roughly%200.8%20s%20each%2C%20are%20already%20smoothed%20versions%20of%20the%20truth%20%E2%80%94%20they%20cannot%20show%20the%20within-stride%20fluctuation%20that%20the%20laser%20radar%20records.%20The%20accelerations%2C%20being%20differences%20of%20those%20differences%2C%20are%20the%20roughest%20estimate%20in%20the%20figure%3A%20the%20acceleration%20panel%20jumps%20around%20in%20a%20way%20that%20no%20human%20body%20actually%20did.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20error%20is%20not%20only%20random%2C%20either.%20Look%20at%20the%20peak%20acceleration%20the%20code%20printed%3A%20a%20little%20over%203%20m%2Fs%C2%B2.%20A%20sprinter%20leaving%20the%20blocks%20actually%20reaches%20something%20closer%20to%208-10%20m%2Fs%C2%B2%2C%20and%20our%20estimate%20misses%20it%20by%20a%20factor%20of%20three%20%E2%80%94%20not%20because%20the%20arithmetic%20is%20wrong%2C%20but%20because%20the%20first%20split%20spans%201.88%20s%20and%20the%20whole%20explosive%20start%20is%20averaged%20away%20inside%20it.%20**A%20finite%20difference%20cannot%20resolve%20anything%20faster%20than%20its%20own%20interval.**%20If%20you%20had%20predicted%20a%20number%20near%20gravity%20before%20running%20the%20cell%2C%20you%20were%20closer%20to%20the%20truth%20than%20the%20data%20were.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Neither%20problem%20is%20a%20flaw%20in%20our%20arithmetic.%20Differentiating%20measured%20data%20amplifies%20whatever%20error%20is%20in%20it%2C%20every%20time%20you%20do%20it%2C%20and%20smooths%20away%20whatever%20is%20briefer%20than%20the%20sampling%20interval.%20It%20is%20the%20reason%20the%20notebooks%20on%20%5Bdata%20filtering%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fdata_filtering.py)%20and%20%5Bresidual%20analysis%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fresidual_analysis.py)%20exist%2C%20and%20the%20reason%20experienced%20people%20are%20suspicious%20of%20any%20acceleration%20curve%20computed%20from%20position%20data.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Challenge%206.**%20Work%20these%20with%20the%20functions%20above.%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Was%20Bolt's%20acceleration%20constant%20over%20any%20part%20of%20the%20race%3F%20Look%20at%20the%20acceleration%20panel%2C%20then%20at%20the%20velocity%20panel%2C%20and%20decide%20which%20one%20gives%20you%20a%20more%20trustworthy%20answer.%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Fit%20a%20straight%20line%20to%20the%20first%20three%20velocity%20points%20and%20use%20its%20slope%20as%20an%20estimate%20of%20the%20initial%20acceleration.%20How%20does%20it%20compare%20to%20the%20peak%20in%20the%20acceleration%20panel%3F%20Which%20would%20you%20report%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20The%20first%20segment%20includes%20about%200.15%20s%20of%20reaction%20time.%20Recompute%20the%20first%20velocity%20using%20the%20actual%20movement%20time%20instead%20of%20the%20split%20time.%20How%20much%20does%20it%20change%3F%0A%20%20%20%204.%20Add%20Gay%20(9.71%20s)%20and%20Powell%20(9.84%20s)%20from%20the%20split%20table%20above%20and%20plot%20all%20three%20velocity%20curves%20together.%20Where%20in%20the%20race%20was%20the%20race%20actually%20decided%3F%0A%20%20%20%205.%20Bolt's%20peak%20velocity%20is%20around%2012.3%20m%2Fs.%20If%20he%20could%20have%20held%20exactly%20that%20from%20the%20gun%2C%20what%20would%20his%20time%20have%20been%3F%20What%20does%20the%20gap%20between%20that%20and%209.58%20s%20tell%20you%20about%20where%20sprint%20performance%20is%20won%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20**Exercise%203.**%20A%20particle%20starts%20at%20rest%20with%20%24a(t)%3D2t%24%20m%2Fs%C2%B2.%20Find%20velocity%20and%20displacement%20at%202%20s.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%20details%20%7C%20Worked%20solution%20%E2%80%94%20Exercise%203%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Integrating%20gives%20%24v%3Dt%5E2%24%20and%20%24x-x_0%3Dt%5E3%2F3%24.%20At%202%20s%20these%20are%204%20m%2Fs%20and%20%248%2F3%24%20m.%20The%20initial%20conditions%20determine%20the%20otherwise%20missing%20integration%20constants.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Checkpoint%20questions%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Pause%20here%20before%20the%20problems.%20These%20connect%20this%20notebook%20to%20the%20rest%20of%20the%20collection.%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20You%20are%20given%20position%20data%20and%20you%20need%20acceleration.%20You%20are%20given%20acceleration%20data%20and%20you%20need%20position.%20Which%20of%20the%20two%20situations%20is%20more%20dangerous%2C%20and%20why%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20A%20marker%20on%20a%20walking%20person's%20heel%20is%20tracked%20at%20100%20Hz.%20What%20is%20the%20shortest%20event%20you%20could%20hope%20to%20resolve%20in%20its%20velocity%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20Why%20is%20the%20average%20velocity%20of%20a%20100%20m%20sprinter%20a%20poor%20description%20of%20the%20race%2C%20while%20the%20average%20velocity%20of%20a%20marathon%20runner%20is%20a%20reasonable%20one%3F%0A%20%20%20%204.%20An%20accelerometer%20on%20a%20phone%20records%20a%20person%20jumping.%20What%20two%20pieces%20of%20information%2C%20not%20in%20the%20accelerometer%20signal%2C%20do%20you%20need%20before%20you%20can%20say%20how%20high%20they%20jumped%3F%0A%20%20%20%205.%20In%20which%20of%20these%20is%20the%20particle%20model%20adequate%2C%20and%20in%20which%20does%20it%20break%20down%3A%20the%20flight%20of%20a%20long%20jumper%2C%20the%20rotation%20of%20a%20diver%2C%20the%20path%20of%20a%20wheelchair%2C%20the%20swing%20of%20a%20golf%20club%3F%0A%20%20%20%206.%20Displacement%20and%20distance%20coincide%20for%20the%20100%20m%20dash.%20Name%20a%20movement%20in%20your%20own%20field%20where%20they%20differ%20substantially%2C%20and%20say%20which%20one%20you%20would%20report.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Problems%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Consider%20the%20data%20for%20the%20three%20medalists%20of%20the%20100%20m%20dash%20in%20Berlin%2C%202009%2C%20shown%20in%20the%2020%20m%20split%20table%20above.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20a.%20Calculate%20interval%20velocities%20and%20accelerations%20with%20%60split_kinematics%60%3B%20define%20average%20acceleration%20between%20the%20first%20and%20last%20velocity%20midpoints.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20b.%20Plot%20the%20graphs%20for%20the%20displacement%2C%20velocity%2C%20and%20acceleration%20versus%20time.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20c.%20Plot%20the%20graphs%20of%20velocity%20and%20acceleration%20versus%20partial%20distance%20(every%2020%20m).%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20d.%20Calculate%20the%20average%20velocity%20and%20average%20acceleration%2C%20and%20the%20instants%20and%20values%20of%20the%20peak%20velocity%20and%20peak%20acceleration.%0A%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Repeat%20the%20calculations%20of%20problem%202%20with%20the%2010%20m%20split%20times%20of%20Graubner%20and%20Nixdorf%2C%20reusing%20the%20functions%20written%20above%2C%20and%20compare%20the%20results.%20The%20two%20published%20tables%20also%20differ%20slightly%20in%20some%20split%20times%3B%20distinguish%20those%20source%20differences%20from%20sampling%20effects.%20Which%20quantities%20change%20most%20when%20the%20distance%20interval%20is%20halved%20%E2%80%94%20position%2C%20velocity%2C%20or%20acceleration%3F%20Relate%20your%20answer%20to%20the%20discussion%20of%20finite%20differences%20above.%0A%0A%20%20%20%203.%20On%20an%20Olympic%20running%20track%2C%20runners%20A%20and%20B%20start%20running%20on%20the%20first%20lane%20(the%20inside%20lane)%20from%20the%20same%20position%20on%20the%20track%2C%20but%20in%20opposite%20directions.%20If%20%24%5ClVert%20v_A%20%5CrVert%20%3D%204%24%20m%2Fs%20and%20%24%5ClVert%20v_B%20%5CrVert%20%3D%206%24%20m%2Fs%2C%20how%20far%20from%20the%20starting%20line%20will%20the%20runners%20meet%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%204.%20A%20body%20attached%20to%20a%20spring%20has%20its%20position%20(in%20cm)%20described%20by%20the%20equation%20%24x(t)%20%3D%202%5Csin(4%5Cpi%20t%20%2B%20%5Cpi%2F4)%24.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20a.%20Calculate%20the%20equations%20for%20the%20body's%20velocity%20and%20acceleration.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20b.%20Plot%20the%20position%2C%20velocity%2C%20and%20acceleration%20in%20the%20interval%20%24%5B0%2C%201%5D%24%20s.%0A%0A%20%20%20%205.%20The%20rectilinear%20motion%20of%20a%20particle%20is%20given%20by%20%24x(t)%20%3D%20-12t%5E3%20%2B%2015t%5E2%20%2B%205t%20%2B%202%24%20%5Bs%3B%20m%5D.%20Calculate%3A%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20a.%20Velocity%20and%20acceleration%20of%20the%20particle%20as%20functions%20of%20time.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20b.%20Total%20distance%20traveled%20by%20the%20particle%20in%20the%20interval%20%240%20%5Cleq%20t%20%5Cleq%204%24%20s.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20c.%20Maximum%20value%20of%20the%20velocity%20magnitude%20reached%20by%20the%20particle%20in%20the%20interval%20%240%20%5Cleq%20t%20%5Cleq%204%24%20s.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20d.%20Plots%20of%20the%20position%2C%20velocity%20and%20acceleration%20of%20the%20particle%20in%20the%20interval%20%240%20%5Cleq%20t%20%5Cleq%204%24%20s.%0A%0A%20%20%20%206.%20A%20stone%20is%20released%20from%20the%20opening%20of%20a%20well%2C%20and%20the%20noise%20of%20its%20fall%20reaching%20the%20bottom%20is%20heard%204%20seconds%20later.%20Knowing%20that%20the%20speed%20of%20sound%20in%20air%20is%20340%20m%2Fs%2C%20determine%20the%20depth%20of%20the%20well.%0A%0A%20%20%20%207.%20The%20position%20of%20a%20particle%20is%20given%20by%20%24%5Coverrightarrow%7B%5Cmathbf%7Br%7D%7D(t)%20%3D%20t%5E2%5C%2C%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bi%7D%7D%20%2B%20e%5E%7Bt%7D%5C%2C%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bj%7D%7D%24.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20a.%20Calculate%20the%20velocity%20and%20acceleration%20of%20the%20particle%20as%20functions%20of%20time.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20b.%20Draw%20the%20path%20of%20the%20particle%20and%20show%20the%20vectors%20%24%5Coverrightarrow%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bv%7D%7D(t)%24%20and%20%24%5Coverrightarrow%7B%5Cmathbf%7Ba%7D%7D(t)%24%20at%20%24t%20%3D%201%24%20s.%0A%0A%20%20%20%208.%20Sometimes%20all%20you%20have%20is%20an%20image%20of%20the%20data%20you%20want.%20The%20first%20figure%20in%20this%20notebook%20contains%20velocity-versus-position%20data%20for%20Bolt's%20sprint%20at%20a%20much%20higher%20resolution%20than%20the%20split%20times%20we%20used.%20Software%20exists%20to%20recover%20numbers%20from%20such%20images%20by%20identifying%20points%20of%20interest%2C%20automatically%20where%20possible%20and%20manually%20where%20not%3B%20%5BWebPlotDigitizer%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fautomeris.io%2FWebPlotDigitizer%2F)%20is%20one%20such%20tool.%20Use%20it%20to%20extract%20the%20data%20from%20that%20figure%20and%20compare%20the%20result%20with%20the%20velocity%20curve%20you%20computed.%20It%20will%20not%20be%20easy%20%E2%80%94%20that%20is%20part%20of%20the%20lesson.%0A%0A%20%20%20%209.%20There%20is%20good%20free%20software%20for%20the%20kinematic%20analysis%20of%20human%20motion%2C%20among%20them%20%5BKinovea%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fwww.kinovea.org%2F)%2C%20%5BTracker%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fphyslets.org%2Ftracker%2F)%2C%20and%20SkillSpector%20(a%20historical%20program%20in%20the%20original%20tutorial%3B%20its%20former%20vendor%20link%20is%20no%20longer%20a%20reliable%20installation%20source).%20Visit%20their%20websites%20and%20work%20out%20which%20biomechanical%20applications%20each%20is%20suited%20to.%0A%0A%20%20%20%2010.%20Return%20to%20the%20movement%20you%20chose%20in%20Challenge%200.%20Write%20one%20paragraph%3A%20which%20kinematic%20quantity%20would%20answer%20your%20question%2C%20how%20you%20would%20measure%20it%2C%20how%20many%20times%20per%20second%20you%20would%20have%20to%20sample%20it%2C%20and%20whether%20you%20would%20have%20to%20differentiate%20or%20integrate%20to%20get%20there.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%20details%20%7C%20Final%20answers%20to%20the%20problems%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20With%20the%2020%20m%20tables%20and%20midpoint%20convention%2C%20the%20final%20velocities%20(m%2Fs)%20are%3A%20Bolt%20%5B6.9444%2C%2011.3636%2C%2011.9760%2C%2012.4224%2C%2012.0482%5D%3B%20Gay%20%5B6.8493%2C%2011.2360%2C%2011.8343%2C%2012.2699%2C%2011.8343%5D%3B%20Powell%20%5B6.8729%2C%2011.1111%2C%2011.6959%2C%2011.9048%2C%2011.4943%5D.%20Acceleration%20arrays%20(m%2Fs%C2%B2)%3A%20Bolt%20%5B1.9048%2C%200.3571%2C%200.2721%2C%20%E2%88%920.2288%5D%3B%20Gay%20%5B1.8667%2C%200.3449%2C%200.2624%2C%20%E2%88%920.2624%5D%3B%20Powell%20%5B1.7997%2C%200.3332%2C%200.1232%2C%20%E2%88%920.2401%5D.%20Mean%20race%20speeds%20are%2010.4384%2C%2010.2987%20and%2010.1626%20m%2Fs.%20Mean%20accelerations%20between%20velocity%20midpoints%20are%200.6982%2C%200.6732%20and%200.6150%20m%2Fs%C2%B2.%20Peak%20speeds%20occur%20at%207.115%2C%207.205%20and%207.260%20s%3B%20peak%20estimated%20accelerations%20at%202.600%2C%202.635%20and%202.6325%20s.%20These%20coarse%20estimates%20do%20not%20recover%20instantaneous%20starting%20acceleration.%0A%20%20%20%202.%20For%20the%2010%20m%20table%3A%20mean%20race%20speeds%20are%20unchanged%3B%20peak%20speeds%20are%20Bolt%2012.3457%20m%2Fs%20at%206.695%20s%2C%20Gay%2012.1951%20m%2Fs%20at%205.950%20s%2C%20and%20Powell%2011.9048%20m%2Fs%20over%20both%2050%E2%80%9360%20and%2060%E2%80%9370%20m.%20Peak%20estimated%20accelerations%20are%203.2506%2C%203.1183%20and%203.0929%20m%2Fs%C2%B2.%20Acceleration%20changes%20most.%20The%20source%20tables%20have%20slightly%20different%20split%20estimates%2C%20so%20the%20difference%20is%20not%20solely%20sampling%20resolution.%0A%20%20%20%203.%20After%2040%20s%3B%20160%20m%20along%20A%E2%80%99s%20direction%2C%20or%20240%20m%20along%20B%E2%80%99s%20direction.%0A%20%20%20%204.%20%24v%3D8%5Cpi%5Ccos(4%5Cpi%20t%2B%5Cpi%2F4)%24%20cm%2Fs%3B%20%24a%3D-32%5Cpi%5E2%5Csin(4%5Cpi%20t%2B%5Cpi%2F4)%24%20cm%2Fs%C2%B2.%20The%20period%20is%200.5%20s%2C%20so%20the%20requested%20interval%20contains%20two%20cycles%3B%20acceleration%20is%20opposite%20in%20sign%20to%20position%20and%20velocity%20is%20shifted%20by%20a%20quarter-cycle.%0A%20%20%20%205.%20%24v%3D-36t%5E2%2B30t%2B5%24%20m%2Fs%3B%20%24a%3D-72t%2B30%24%20m%2Fs%C2%B2.%20Total%20distance%20is%20approximately%20524.017%20m%3B%20peak%20speed%20is%20451%20m%2Fs%20at%204%20s.%20The%20position%20has%20one%20turning%20point%20within%20the%20interval%2C%20at%20%24t%3D(5%2B3%5Csqrt5)%2F12%5Capprox0.97568%24%20s.%0A%20%20%20%206.%20%24h%5Capprox70.552%24%20m%20for%20%24g%3D9.81%24%20m%2Fs%C2%B2%2C%20including%20the%20sound%20travel%20time.%0A%20%20%20%207.%20%24%5Cmathbf%20v%3D(2t%2Ce%5Et)%24%2C%20%24%5Cmathbf%20a%3D(2%2Ce%5Et)%24.%20At%201%20s%3A%20position%20%24(1%2Ce)%24%2C%20velocity%20%24(2%2Ce)%24%2C%20acceleration%20%24(2%2Ce)%24%20in%20the%20corresponding%20SI%20units.%20The%20path%20is%20%24y%3De%5E%7B%5Csqrt%20x%7D%24%20for%20%24t%5Cge0%24.%0A%20%20%20%208.%20Digitized%20estimates%20depend%20on%20calibration%20and%20selected%20pixels.%20A%20credible%20result%20is%20a%20positive%20speed%20curve%20peaking%20around%2012%E2%80%9312.5%20m%2Fs%20near%2060%E2%80%9370%20m%20and%20declining%20toward%20the%20finish%2C%20with%20stated%20axis%20calibration%20and%20digitization%20uncertainty.%0A%20%20%20%209.%20Kinovea%20supports%20practical%20calibrated%20video%20measurements%3B%20Tracker%20supports%20point%20tracking%20and%20physics%20models.%20SkillSpector%20is%20retained%20as%20a%20historical%20comparison%2C%20not%20a%20current%20installation%20recommendation.%20Select%20by%20calibration%2C%20frame%20rate%2C%20dimensionality%2C%20visibility%20and%20export%20needs%2C%20and%20check%20the%20maintained%20project%20documentation.%0A%20%20%20%2010.%20Answers%20depend%20on%20the%20chosen%20movement.%20A%20complete%20response%20specifies%20the%20quantity%2C%20reference%20frame%2C%20units%2C%20sensor%2C%20sampling%20interval%2C%20and%20whether%20differentiation%20or%20integration%20is%20required%2C%20with%20the%20initial%20conditions%20or%20noise%20treatment%20that%20operation%20needs.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20More%20examples%0A%0A%20%20%20%20-%20From%20Ruina%20and%20Pratap's%20book%2C%20study%20samples%2012.2%20and%2012.3.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo%2C%20np%2C%20plt)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_tables%20%3D%20%7B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%2220%20m%22%3A%20%5B%5B2.88%2C%204.64%2C%206.31%
